To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the attractiveness of static images of female bodies is affected by the posture of the person in the images and that the posture of the observer affects the perception of the attractiveness of the images.
the attractiveness of a person's image is influenced by the posture of the viewer, and that this is true even when viewers are unaware of the posture's relevance.
the perceived attractiveness of a female body is affected by the symmetry of the body, the length of the legs relative to the body, and the posture of the viewer relative to the posture of the body.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of posture in social perception and the role of embodiment in perception of attractiveness.
the relationship between postural congruence of the perceiver and the perceived, and the role of this relationship for the perception of attractiveness.
the role of the viewer's posture in perception of physical attractiveness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the posture of the observer influences the perceived attractiveness of an observed person, and that this effect is stronger for images that are in a similar posture as the observer.
the posture of the viewer influences the perception of physical attractiveness of static images of the viewed person.
the perception of attractiveness of others is affected by the posture of the observer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
attractiveness is a multi-faceted concept and that the attractiveness of a person is influenced by a multitude of factors.
the perception of attractiveness from a static image is influenced by the posture of the person who views it, even if the viewer is unaware of the effect.
the perception of attractiveness is a social interaction, in which the postures of the observer and the observed person influence each others' perceptions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between the posture of the observer and the observed object affects the perception of attractiveness.
our own body posture influences how attractive we perceive a person.
the relationship between the postures of the observer and the viewed person affects the perception of attractiveness, and that this effect is not limited to dynamic stimuli.
